topic: Why can a queue suddenly grow?
prior: May count the person being served as waiting.
objective: Predict waiting count with a fixed service schedule.
takeaway: Arrivals can bunch even when service never slows.

sources.Q1: Fictional FIFO fixture; compute every event from the supplied clock.

editorial_direction: Open on a quiet counter that suddenly looks busy.
misconceptions: A person already served still counts in the line

chapters.question: How fast can the counter serve?
chapter_claims: One FIFO counter; A arrives at zero; fixed two-minute service.
stages: Read the clock and start the first service.
Show B and C arrive at minute one.

chapters.question: What happens at the same minute as a departure?
chapter_claims: At a tie, complete service, start the next waiting person, then add new arrivals. D arrives at minute two.
stages: Hold minute one while posing the next event.
Reveal B serving and C, D waiting.

chapters.question: Did service speed change when the line grew?
chapter_claims: Service is fixed at two minutes. At minute four A and B have departed, C serves, D waits. All depart by eight.
stages: Show the last person departed at minute eight.

chapters.question: What if D comes a minute later?
chapter_claims: Change only D's arrival to minute three. At minute two B serves and C alone waits.

transfer.question: If D arrives at minute three instead, who is waiting just after minute two?
transfer.answer: Only C. B is being served; D hasn’t arrived.
